findings.title: Single SendGrid failure aborts cancellation of entire batch and loses already-cancelled reminders
findings.body: The for-loop that cancels pending email reminders (lines 56-73) is wrapped in a single try/catch around the whole loop. If `client.request` throws for any one reminder (e.g. an invalid/expired batch_id), the loop stops immediately: (1) all subsequent reminders in `remindersToCancel` are skipped for this cron run even though their scheduledDate may be within the next hour, meaning their emails can still be sent — the exact bug this PR is meant to fix; (2) `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls created for reminders that WERE successfully cancelled earlier in the loop are Prisma 'thenable' lazy promises that only execute when awaited via `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)`. Since the exception short-circuits execution before that `await Promise.all(...)` line is ever reached, those delete operations never actually run, so already-cancelled reminders are never removed from the DB and will be retried (and the SendGrid cancel re-sent) on every subsequent cron run indefinitely. The loop should catch/log errors per-reminder and continue, and each delete should be executed immediately rather than deferred to a batched Promise.all after the loop.

findings.title: immediateDelete branch cancels in SendGrid but never deletes the WorkflowReminder row
findings.body: When `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` is called with `immediateDelete=true` (lines 213-223), it issues the SendGrid 'cancel' request but returns without deleting or updating the corresponding `workflowReminder` row. Unlike the other two branches (no referenceId -> delete immediately; deferred -> set `cancelled: true`), this path leaves the row in the database indefinitely with `scheduled: true` and `cancelled` unset. The row will only be purged later by the unrelated 'delete all scheduled reminders whose scheduledDate is in the past' cleanup in scheduleEmailReminders.ts, meaning stale WorkflowReminder rows linger in the table (potentially for days) referencing an event that has already been cancelled/replaced, polluting any UI or reporting that reads this table.

findings.title: Reschedule flow bypasses the new batched-cancellation mechanism, risking the original SendGrid pending-cancellation cap bug
findings.body: When rescheduling, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called with `immediateDelete=true`, which synchronously calls SendGrid's cancel endpoint right away instead of marking the reminder `cancelled: true` for the throttled CRON-based cancellation introduced by this PR. The PR's stated rationale is that direct/immediate SendGrid cancellations build up against SendGrid's max of 100 pending cancellations and start failing silently, causing reminders to still be sent. By using `immediateDelete=true` here, bulk/rapid rescheduling (e.g. for recurring events or round-robin events) can reintroduce exactly that failure mode for the reschedule flow, even though the booking-cancellation flow (handleCancelBooking.ts) was fixed to defer via the `cancelled` flag.

findings.title: Workflow deletion also bypasses batched cancellation via immediateDelete=true
findings.body: In the `delete` mutation, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true)` is called for every scheduled reminder belonging to a deleted workflow. As with the reschedule path, this issues a direct SendGrid cancel call per reminder instead of deferring to the new CRON-based cancellation (`cancelled: true`) that this PR introduces specifically to avoid hitting SendGrid's max-100-pending-cancellations limit. Deleting a workflow that has many scheduled reminders can trigger many simultaneous direct cancel calls, risking the same silent-failure scenario the PR is fixing elsewhere, and leaves the corresponding rows undeleted in the DB (see emailReminderManager.ts immediateDelete branch) for every immediate call that doesn't fail.

findings.title: SMS reminder DB row is only deleted if twilio.cancelSMS succeeds, unlike previous unconditional deletion
findings.body: Previously, callers (e.g. handleCancelBooking.ts) unconditionally ran `prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany` for every reminder regardless of whether the external cancellation call succeeded. Now `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` performs `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` and `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` inside the same try block; if `twilio.cancelSMS` throws (e.g. invalid/expired SID, Twilio API error), the subsequent delete is skipped and the error is swallowed by the catch block (just logged). This leaves an orphaned WorkflowReminder row in the database for a cancelled/rescheduled booking, with no retry mechanism, which is a regression in data cleanliness compared to the prior behavior.

findings.title: Cancellation query does not scope to EMAIL method despite being EMAIL/SendGrid-specific logic
findings.body: The query for `remindersToCancel` (lines 44-51) filters only on `cancelled: true` and `scheduledDate`, without restricting to `method: WorkflowMethods.EMAIL`. The subsequent code unconditionally treats every matched row as a SendGrid batch (calling the `/v3/user/scheduled_sends` cancel endpoint with `batch_id: reminder.referenceId`). Currently the `cancelled` flag is only ever set for EMAIL reminders, so this works, but the coupling is implicit and fragile — if any future code path sets `cancelled: true` on an SMS reminder, this cron job would incorrectly attempt a SendGrid cancel call against a Twilio reference id.

findings.title: Missing test coverage for the new cancellation/cron logic fixing the reported bug
findings.body: This PR adds a materially new and fairly intricate cancellation flow (cancelled flag set at cancel/reschedule time, consumed by this CRON job up to 1 hour before scheduledDate, interacting with SendGrid's scheduled_sends API) specifically to fix a production bug where reminders for cancelled/rescheduled bookings were still sent. No automated tests were added to validate that cancelled bookings no longer produce sent reminders, that the new `cancelled` flag is correctly set/consumed, or that the batch cancellation endpoint is called with the right parameters, leaving the exact scenario this PR fixes unverified by CI.
